newsitem.title: USA: U.S. drugmaker stocks rise, several hit new highs.
newsitem.headline: U.S. drugmaker stocks rise, several hit new highs.

text.p: Shares of U.S. pharmaceutical companies hit new highs Thursday, taking a cue from a powerful overall stock market and firm earnings trends, analysts said.

As the Dow Jones Industrial Average soared above 7,000 points, nearly all of the major drug companies made new yearly highs, including Merck and Co, Pfizer Inc, Eli Lilly and Co and Bristol-Myers Squibb Co.

"It's overall market strength," said Brian Eisenbarth, an analyst at Collins & Co. "Money continues to flow into that sector because most of the pharmaceutical companies have deep pipelines and strong earnings growth. They are not cheap, but are seen as a quality place to put money."

Merck hit an intraday high for the year of 99-7/8. It closed up 3-7/8 to 99-3/4. Pfizer hit an annual high of 96-3/4, closing up 2-3/8 to 96, while Bristol ended at its annual high of 134-3/4, up 2-7/8. Lilly reached a year high of 93, closing up 2-1/4 at 92-3/4. Warner-Lambert Co also rose to an annual high of 90, finishing up 2-3/4 at 89-7/8.
David Saks, an analyst at Gruntal & Co, raised his rating on Merck, Pfizer and Schering-Plough Corp to strong buy from outperform, based on strong prescription sales data.
"Profit margins and earnings growth are accelerating owing to strong prescription unit volume growth," Saks said in a research note.
The companies' shares would benefit from accelerating earnings and expanding price-to-earnings ratios, he said.

Schering-Plough ended up 1/4 at 79-3/4 after hitting a year-high of 80 intraday. Saks said Schering would outperform due to top-lin sales growth, downsizing costs, share repurchases, strategic deals and market share gains.
Alex Zisson, an analyst at Hambrecht & Quist also attributed the drugmaker's share price rise to a very solid earnings performance in the first quarter.
"I'm not quite sure why there has been a delayed reaction," he said.
